I feel like the market is being manipulated more by political influencers these days than actual economic indicators and that’s why savvy investors are ignoring the hype.  For instance the fear mongering about inflation and raising interest rates.  Typically rates are raised when an overheated economy causes inflation but right now it’s energy costs and not an overheated economy driving a small spike in inflation numbers.  Raising interest rates seems like the wrong lever to pull unless you want to keep the economic fire tamped down for political reasons.  Our economy and country would be better served if interest rates were lowered making money cheaper for small business and the real estate market.  Inflation will take care of itself as market forces increase the supply and lower the cost of energy.  I think stock market investors know this intuitively so they are marching on like it’s all fake news while the rest of the economy is left harnessed by the ebb and flow of politics.

As a long term investor I just keep putting money into my three fund portfolio and know my years worth of expenses in SWVXX and years worth in SGOV will see me through the nonsense.
There’s plenty of political noise, but rising yields and inflation aren’t just partisan hype. Those are separate data points.

How does REITS perform in high interest rate situations
@NolanGouveia-y7n me scam you long time
REITs can face higher interest cost just like all real estate. That could cause discount to equity holding value. More so if long term sustained higher rates.

REITs are getting beat up right now as rising rates are not good for REITs, but I see this as a time to start acquiring positions in some of the better quality REITs and BDCs which are also getting hit right now.

REITs finance a huge portion of their operations thru bonds, and because they must pay 90% of pretaxed income as dividends, they have very little in the way of retained earnings to pay down the debt or expand the business when rates rise. They can benefit from higher rates if rates stay stable for long enough periods of time

Some areas I've been adding to lately are the ones with strong historical returns but recent weakness. SPMD or MDY (S&P 400 Mid Caps) had dropped over 8%, showing the weakness beyond mega-cap tech companies.
